Optimising Compressed Air 
at Nalagarh
At Nalagarh, we redesigned the 
compressed-air distribution system to take on additional machines without installing another compressor. Improving the pipeline configuration let us make better use of existing infrastructure while reducing energy losses. It shows how targeted process optimisation can improve resource efficiency and avoid extra capital spend at the same time.
Energy Optimisation Race 
2025
As part of Sustainability and Mental 
Wellbeing Month 2025, we ran the Energy Optimisation Race, inviting our manufacturing units to showcase energy-conservation projects that deliver measurable operational and sustainability benefits.
Projects were evaluated on energy 
savings, innovation, scalability, environmental impact and operational efficiency. Following a multi-stage evaluation, Vasind, Manpura and EPTB emerged as the leading units.
The projects included pumping-system 
optimisation, solar-powered cooling, improvements to compressed-air and chilled-water systems, smart lighting controls and vacuum-system upgrades. Beyond recognition, the race gave us a way to share employee-led ideas and scale proven ones across locations.Accelerating Energy Efficiency through Kaizen
A three-day Energy Kaizen programme at Vapi (India) brought together cross-functional teams, portfolio-company representatives and external specialists to identify high-impact efficiency opportunities.
The exercise identified 14 energy-saving projects, of which four were completed 
during the year. Opportunities included chiller and cooling-system optimisation, compressed-air and HVAC improvements, smart lighting, thermal insulation, advanced energy monitoring, IoT-enabled controls and renewable-energy integration.

Transitioning to Lower-Impact Refrigerants
We are steadily phasing down high Global Warming Potential refrigerants and adopting lower-impact alternatives such as ammonia, CO₂ and hydrocarbons. This complements our energy-efficiency and renewable-energy work by tackling another important source of operational climate impact.
EPL implements preventive inspection and maintenance practices to identify and 
address leaks from pipes, valves, hoses, seals, solvent-handling systems and other potential fugitive emission sources. Identified leaks are promptly repaired and records are maintained to ensure equipment integrity and minimise fugitive emissions.

Water Stewardship
Water is an important input across 
manufacturing processes, particularly cooling and printing. The Company sources water through natural wells, canals and public supply systems., 
Water Risk assessment
Our facilities are strategically located outside water stress zone, as confirmed by our FY 2025-26 water risk assessment as per WRI (World Resource Institute aqueduct tool).
EPL conducts water basin risk 
assessments for its manufacturing sites to identify potential operational and financial impacts arising from local water-related risks. Assessments consider water scarcity, groundwater depletion, drought and incoming water quality, enabling EPL to identify vulnerable locations and implement appropriate water conservation, recycling and business-continuity measures.
A closed-loop system keeps water 
recirculating between primary circuits, covering chillers, cooling towers and pumps, and secondary circuits serving production equipment. All our facilities also run Sewage Treatment Plants, so treated water can be reused in landscaping and sanitation.
Water Quality and Control
We routinely monitor water-quality parameters including pH, Total Dissolved Solids, turbidity, chlorides and microbiological indicators, together with groundwater contaminants such as heavy metals. To prevent contamination, we enforce secure wastewater discharge, eliminate floor drains where possible, and maintain on-site septic systems. In FY 2025-26, EPL maintained zero pollutant emissions, ensuring no water contamination.
Controls include secure wastewater-
discharge systems, removal of floor drains where feasible, on-site septic systems and GMP-led water audits to identify leaks and improve water efficiency.
Exceeding the 2030 Water Recycling Target
The Company had committed to recycling 50% of water by 2030, against a baseline of 22% in 2021.
During FY 2025-26, the water-recycling rate reached 55%, surpassing the 2030 
target ahead of schedule. The Company recycled and reused 100 ML of water, while total water consumption stood at 183 ML.

We keep air emissions from operations under regular monitoring and regulatory control.  EPL aims to achieve zero air-pollution non-compliance cases annually and maintain this performance through 2030 against baseline of 2022. In addition, EPL targets 100% of its operational sites to maintain air-emission monitoring values within the applicable limits prescribed by local regulations each year, with the same target maintained through 2030 against baseline of 2022.
Noise Reduction
EPL maintains a preventive maintenance program for noise-generating equipment to identify and replace worn or damaged components such as bearings, belts, couplings and other rotating parts before they cause abnormal noise. Regular inspections, timely replacement and equipment maintenance help control workplace noise levels and prevent deterioration of noise performance.
Engineering interventions include equipment speed optimisation, vibration-damping 
materials, acoustic shielding, lower-noise components and quiet-design gear systems.

Partnership with Banyan Nation
The Company continues to collaborate with Banyan Nation to address recycling 
challenges associated with laminate tube structures and improve recovery of post-consumer tube waste.
The partnership pairs our packaging expertise with Banyan Nation’s recycling 
strengths and digital platform to improve material collection, traceability and recycling outcomes.
Key Areas of Collaboration
Collection and Recycling InfrastructureStrengthening collection, segregation and processing systems to support scalable recycling
Data-Driven Traceability
Using digital systems to integrate informal recyclers and improve visibility across recovery networks
High-Quality Recyclate Production
Developing PCR materials suitable for reintegration into mainstream packaging applications
EPR and Regulatory Alignment
Supporting Extended Producer Responsibility requirements and evolving circularity expectations
Together, these interventions are helping develop a more scalable circular 
supply chain for plastic tube packaging.Project Liberty: 
Recovering Value from Complex Laminates
Project Liberty tackles the 
recycling challenges of laminate tubes, particularly structures containing aluminium. Our proprietary separation process recovers polymer and aluminium layers as distinct reusable streams without chemicals or heat.
Recovered polymer can be 
repurposed for applications including blow moulding and injection moulding, while aluminium can be channelled into downstream industrial uses.
During FY 2025-26, Recycled 
3675.638 tonnes of plastic waste via Project Liberty. The programme continued to expand across in-plant, post-industrial and post-consumer recovery streams, strengthening our ability to convert complex laminate waste into reusable resources.

New Generation Recycling technology at Wada enables the recovery and 
reuse of post-industrial plastic waste within operations. Production scrap is converted into reusable material streams, reducing disposal requirements and dependence on virgin inputs.
During FY 2025-26, the facility recycled over 877 MT of post-industrial waste. 
Recovered material is reintegrated into applications including liners, core plugs and polypropylene pallets, strengthening internal material circularity and supporting closed-loop manufacturing.

Protecting Nature through 
Informed Action
We build biodiversity into our 
environmental planning and operational decisions. Plant-level assessments help us identify ecologically sensitive areas and distinguish protected from non-protected zones, supporting responsible land use and helping minimise impacts on surrounding habitats.
Lifecycle Assessments further support 
the evaluation of environmental impacts associated with products, including air emissions, water consumption and potential effects on soil.
Our environmental stewardship also 
reaches into the value chain through supplier expectations and engagement, while conservation initiatives spanning water management, recycling and climate action help reduce pressure on natural resources.
Training programmes and collaboration 
with experts, communities and research institutions further strengthen environmental awareness and contribute to biodiversity conservation across the Company’s operating ecosystem.Advancing Resource Recovery
Circularity initiatives across operations include:
Responsible Chemical 
and Hazardous Material Management
We maintain dedicated hazardous-
waste storage areas at our manufacturing locations in line with applicable Pollution Control Board requirements. Waste is segregated, identified, labelled and stored by classification to reduce handling risks and prevent cross-contamination. Vehicles carrying hazardous materials hold proper explosive licenses. Measures are in place to prevent oil spills and evaporation, safeguarding against land and air contamination.
Material Safety Data Sheets and Safety 
Data Sheets are available for hazardous substances, providing guidance on safe handling, storage, emergency response and disposal.
Secondary containment controls 
potential spills or leaks, while fire-detection systems and emergency-response equipment strengthen site preparedness. We collect, transport, treat, recycle or dispose of hazardous waste through authorised vendors in line with applicable regulatory requirements.Product End-of-Life Management and Circularity
Our responsibility for packaging reaches beyond the manufacturing phase. Formal Extended Producer Responsibility programmes and community-based collection support the recovery of post-consumer packaging and its diversion into verified recycling streams. EPL aims to achieve 100% compliance with applicable regional EPR requirements across all applicable locations annually.
Technical datasheets and recyclability information across the tube portfolio help customers 
make informed decisions regarding material composition, recycling and disposal pathways. Through customer engagement and product stewardship, the Company also encourages adoption of formats compatible with established recycling systems.Zero Waste to

At EPL, we believe sustainable 
growth starts with people and is strengthened through fairness, opportunity and trust. During FY 2025-26, we continued to enhance employee experiences by strengthening systems, building capabilities and fostering inclusion across our global workforce of 6,157 employees.  A key milestone was the launch of ELEVATE, our global people experience platform, bringing performance, goals and learning into a single integrated system. This has improved transparency, employee self-service and development conversations.  Inclusion remains central to our culture. Strength in Silence: The Journey of Sai 
Late
Sai Late joined the Wada plant as an apprentice in 
January 2023. Living with a hearing and speech disability since birth, he brought precision, reliability and a strong work ethic to the floor, and moved into a full-time role within four months. He has continued to work towards his Bachelor's degree alongside the job. What his story shows is how far opportunity and everyday workplace support can carry someone who is given the room to prove themselves.Leading with Purpose: Devaki Tomar
Devaki Tomar joined the Vapi unit as an apprentice and moved into the role of Checker in March 2025. As a person with a disability, she has turned her own experience into a source of support for others, and received a Special Jury Mention for Best Mentor at the PrintWeek Women to Watch Awards 2026.
Through the year, she mentored 15 employees across 
functions, working through structured goal-setting, regular feedback and development plans built around each individual, which has helped them take on wider responsibilities and move into new roles with confidence. Her work has also opened up franker conversation about accessibility and inclusion on the shop floor.

Our internal policies are aligned to global standards and supported by regular training on unconscious bias and inclusion. Platforms

Empowering Diverse Abilities
We are building accessibility, innovation and equity into our manufacturing and people practices, so that persons with disabilities can take part fully, contribute and build lasting careers with us.
In FY 2025-26 we employed 155 persons with disabilities 
across seven countries, 117 of them in India, and opened new inclusion initiatives in the USA and Colombia. By FY 2026-27 we intend to carry PwD representation into every global unit, with a larger share of that participation in technical and operational roles.
Project Sanvaad
Project Sanvaad is a digitally enabled sign-language 
interpretation platform running across six plants with the support of more than 50 interpreters. It carries real-time communication into production meetings, safety briefings and training sessions, so employees with hearing impairments take part on the same terms as everyone else.
Complementary interventions include:
 Visual and vibration-based emergency alert systems
 Live-captioning tools
 Accessible learning formats Indian Sign Language training, completed by more 
than 500 employees
 Buddy and Men tor Programme
 A dedicated PwD skill matrix that matches capability 
to role
 Capability-building programmes with external 
partners, including the Red Cross Association
This work is governed through ISO 45001 certified safety 
systems, SEDEX compliance, our Disability and Inclusion Policy, leadership oversight from the Diversity and Inclusion Council and the Speak Up platform.

Advancing Employee 
Wellbeing through Water, Sanitation and Hygiene
Access to safe drinking water, 
sanitation and hygiene is fundamental to employee health, dignity and safe working conditions. WASH considerations are integrated into workplace-management practices and support the Human Rights Policy, Policy on Labour Relations and Working Conditions and the broader sustainability framework.
As a signatory to the WASH Pledge, 
EPL is committed to strengthening access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene facilities across workplaces under its operational control, while supporting the principles of the CEO Water Mandate’s WASH initiatives. Physical and Psychological Safety
A strong workplace is built on both physical safety and psychological safety. Physical safety creates confidence to work without hesitation, while psychological safety gives employees the freedom to think differently, speak openly and learn without fear.
Held together, these principles build trust, accountability 
and personal ownership. Where people feel secure in how they work, think and contribute, they bring more of themselves to the job, and the organisation that results is the stronger for it.

Upholding Human Rights Across Our 
Operations
Respect for human rights underpins the Company’s approach 
to employment and responsible business conduct. 
Employees receive training covering:
The Company respects the principle of  freedom of association 
and collective bargaining, supported through Works Committees and periodically reviewed collective bargaining arrangements. This agreement covers essential aspects such as wages, working hours, overtime, leaves, employee health and safety, working conditions, training and career development, and the prevention of discrimination and harassment. Established in compliance with national laws and regulations, these agreements are negotiated between the company and employee-elected representatives. EPL is committed to achieving 100% employee coverage under collective bargaining agreements annually across all applicable locations.Addressing and Preventing Workplace Violations : 
EPL has a comprehensive remediation procedure to address 
cases of discrimination and harassment, ensuring timely and appropriate action for any violations. This includes transparent communication with stakeholders and ongoing monitoring to assess the effectiveness of corrective measures. EPL ensures security personnel are trained on responsible use of force, human rights, freedom of movement and appropriate security protocols, with clear guidelines on the limits of their authority and periodic monitoring to prevent excessive or unnecessary use of force.
Protecting Against Child Labour, Forced Labour, and Human 
Trafficking :
Preventive safeguards include age verification during 
recruitment, prohibition of recruitment fees, controls concerning identity-document retention. We conduct dedicated worker voice surveys to assess and identify any risks related to these issues. In the rare event that child labour is discovered, we collaborate with local NGOs to provide necessary support and remediation. EPL is committed to ensuring zero cases of child labour and forced labour every year. EPL conducts due diligence on recruitment agencies to ensure ethical recruitment, legal compliance, transparent worker contracts and zero recruitment fees charged to workers, with periodic monitoring of recruitment practices.
Speak Up: Empowering Employees to Raise Their Voice
The Speak Up Policy provides employees and stakeholders with a confidential channel to raise concerns without fear of retaliation.

INDEPENDENT  ASSURANCE  STATEMENT  
 
Independent Assurance Statement to EPL Limited on its Sustainability Report for the FY 2025 -26 
The Board of Directors and Management  
EPL Limited  
Times  Tower,  Kamala  City, 
Senapati  Bapat Marg,  Lower  Parel,  Mumbai  – 400013  
 
Nature of the Assurance  
SGS India Private Limited (hereinafter referred to as SGS India) was commissioned by EPL Limited (the ‘Company’) 
to conduct an independent assurance of its Sustainability Report pertaining to the reporting period of April 1, 2025, to 
March 31, 2026. The Report is prepared based on Global Reporting Initiative (“GRI”) and its Comprehensive option of 
Reporting, covering the performance of the Company across environmental, social and governance (ESG) indicators. 
This assurance engagement was conducted in accordance with “International Standard on Assurance Engagements 
(ISAE) 3000 (Revised)”.  
 
Responsibilities  
The information in the Sustainability Report and its presentation are the responsibility of the directors or governing 
body and the Management of the Company. SGS India has not been involved in the preparation of any of the 
material topics included in the report.  
Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the text, data, graphs, and statements within the defined scope of 
assurance, aiming to inform the Management of the Company, and in alignment with the agreed terms of reference. 
We do not accept or assume any responsibility beyond this specific purpose, and it is not intended for use in 
interpreting the overall performance of the Company, except for the aspects explicitly mentioned within the scope.  
 
Assurance Standard  
This engagement was performed in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagement (ISAE) 
3000 (Revised) (Assurance Engagements other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information) and the 
GRI’s Principles for Defining Report Content and Report Quality. Our evidence -gathering procedures were designed 
to obtain a ‘Reasonable’ level of assurance, which is a high level of assurance but is not absolute certainty. It involves 
obtaining sufficient appropriate evidence to support the conclusion that the information presented in the Sustainability 
Report is fairly stated and is free from material misstatements.  
 
Scope of Assurance  
The assurance process involved assessing the quality, accuracy, and reliability of specific key performance indicators 
(KPIs) within the Sustainability Report for the period spanning April 1, 2025, to March 31, 2026. The reporting scope 
and boundaries include EPL's operational sites across the United States, Mexico, Colombia, Poland, Germany, 
Egypt, China, the Philippines, Brazil, Thailand and India.  
 
The assurance covered the following sample locations for the assessment:  
 
• On-site verification  of data and control  systems  at the following  manufacturing  locations:  
1. EPL Limited – Wada Plant, India.  
2. EPL Limited – Vapi Plant, India.  
Page  2 of 5  
 3. EPL Limited – Vasind Plant, India.  
ϰ͘ EPL Limited – Head Office, India. 

• Virtual  verification  through  screen sharing  tools  at the following  selected  sample  locations:  
1. EPL Limited - Laminate Packaging Colombia S AS 
2. EPL Limited - EPL Propack Philippines Inc . 
 
Assurance Methodology  
The assurance comprised a combination of desktop review, interaction with the key personnel engaged in the 
process of developing the Sustainability Report, on site visits, and remote verification of data. Specifically, SGS India 
undertook the following activities:  
• Examined EPL's strategy for stakeholder engagement and the process of determining materiality, as outlined in 
the Sustainability Report.  
• Conducted interviews with key personnels overseeing sustainability aspects within the company and assessed 
supporting evidence presented in the report.  
• Evaluated the data management system employed for collecting and collating sustainability related information at 
the site level, as well as the consolidation of data at the Head Office level.  
• Verified the consistency of data and information presented within the report and cross -referenced it with the 
source materials.  
 
Limitations  
SGS India did not come across any limitation to the agreed  scope of the assurance engagement. SGS India verified 
data on a sample basis; the responsibility for the authenticity of the data entirely lies with the Company. Financial 
data drawn directly from independently audited financial accounts has not been checked back to source as part of 
this assurance process. The assurance scope excluded forward -looking statements, product - or service -related 
information, external information sources, and expert opinions.  
 
Findings and Conclusions  
Based  on the methodology  described  and the verification  work  performed,  we are satisfied  that the information  
presented  by the Company in its Sustainability Report, on the specified KPIs (listed below) is accurate, reliable, has 
been fairly stated and prepared, in all material respects and is prepared in line with the GRI standard requirements.  
 
The list of KPIs  that were  verified  within  this assurance  engagement  is given  below:

Management Discussion and Analysis
The Directors are pleased to present the Management Discussion and Analysis for the financial year ended on March 31, 2026 (“Financial 
Year 2025-26”/ “FY26”/ “year under review”).
1. ABOUT EPL
  EPL Limited (“EPL ” or “the Company”), is a global specialty packaging company and the world’s leading manufacturer of laminated 
tubes. For over four decades, the Company has partnered with leading global and regional FMCG brands to deliver innovative, high-quality and sustainable packaging solutions across Oral Care, Beauty & Cosmetics, Pharmaceuticals, Food & Nutrition and Home Care.
  With a global manufacturing footprint spanning more than 21 facilities across 11 countries and a workforce of over 6,000 employees, 
EPL serves customers across more than 80 countries through a network that combines global scale with strong local execution. This diversified presence enables the Company to remain close to customers, respond quickly to changing market needs and deliver consistent quality and service across geographies.
  Innovation and sustainability remain central to EPL’s long-term strategy. The Company is investing in advanced packaging 
technologies, differentiated product offerings and sustainable solutions that help customers meet evolving consumer preferences and regulatory requirements. During FY26, these efforts were recognised with an EcoVadis Platinum rating, placing EPL among the top 1% of companies assessed globally for ESG performance.
  FY26 also marked an important strategic milestone with the announcement of the proposed merger with Indovida India Private Limited 
backed by Indorama Ventures. Subject to the necessary shareholder, regulatory and other approvals, the proposed combination is expected to create a diversified consumer packaging platform with an expanded product portfolio, broader geographic reach and enhanced growth opportunities across emerging markets. The proposed transaction is discussed in greater detail in Section 8 of this MD&A.
2. ECONOMIC OVERVIEW AND OUTLOOK
  FY26 was characterised by a resilient but evolving global economic environment. Global GDP growth remained at approximately 
3.3% during calendar year 2025, supported by easing inflation, resilient consumer demand and improving financial conditions across several major economies. However, geopolitical tensions in the Middle East during the latter part of the year heightened uncertainty, leading the IMF to revise its 2026 global growth forecast to approximately 3.1%, while highlighting risks from higher energy prices, supply chain disruptions and tighter financial conditions.
  Growth trends varied across regions. India continued to be the fastest-growing major economy, with GDP growth projected at  
6.3-6.5%, supported by strong domestic demand and manufacturing activity. Consumption trends also improved during the latter part of the year, aided by easing inflation, supportive government measures and a gradual recovery in rural demand. China remained resilient with growth of around 4.4-4.5%, aided by continued policy support, while Europe continued to witness a subdued recovery amid weak industrial activity and moderating inflation. The impact of the ongoing geopolitical uncertainty is expected to be more pronounced across the Middle East and other energy-importing emerging economies, where elevated energy and logistics costs may weigh on growth and inflation.
  Despite these near-term uncertainties, the long-term fundamentals of the packaging industry remain favourable. Demand is 
supported by resilient consumption across essential categories such as Oral Care, Pharmaceuticals and Food, while sustainability, premiumisation and innovation continue to reshape customer requirements and create new growth opportunities in categories like Beauty and Cosmetics.
  Against this backdrop, EPL’s diversified manufacturing footprint, regional operating model and disciplined execution provide the 
agility to respond to changing market conditions while maintaining supply continuity and protecting profitability.
3. INDUSTRY  OVERVIEW
  According to Mordor Intelligence, the global packaging industry is expected to grow at a CAGR of approximately 3-4% over the next five 
years. Growth continues to be supported by rising consumption across personal care, pharmaceuticals, food and home care categories, increasing urbanisation and the expansion of organised retail and e-commerce. As consumer preferences evolve, packaging is increasingly viewed not only as a protective medium but also as a key enabler of brand differentiation, convenience and sustainability.
  Sustainability r emains the most significant structural trend shaping the industry. Mordor Intelligence estimates the global sustainable 
packaging market to grow at a CAGR of approximately 7-8%, significantly outpacing the broader packaging industry. Increasing regulatory focus on recyclability, Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) frameworks and brand commitments towards circular packaging are accelerating the adoption of recyclable, mono-material and post-consumer recycled packaging solutions.

EPL Limited

Management Discussion and Analysis (contd.) Within the packaging industry, flexible packaging continues to outpace overall market growth, driven by lower material consumption, 
a reduced carbon footprint and greater design flexibility. The Beauty & Cosmetics segment continues to witness strong momentum 
as brands increasingly seek premium, aesthetically differentiated and sustainable packaging solutions. These trends are well aligned with EPL’s strategic focus on expanding its presence in Beauty & Cosmetics while strengthening its leadership in Oral Care and other Personal Care categories.
 At the same time, customers increasingly value partners that can combine innovation, global manufacturing capabilities and reliable 
supply with local responsiveness. With its diversified manufacturing footprint, continued investments in technology and sustainability, and long-standing customer relationships, EPL is well positioned to capitalise on these structural growth opportunities.
4. BUSINESS OVER VIEW: FY26
 FY26 marked an important milestone in EPL’s growth journey, with the Company delivering its strongest operating performance in
recent years. Investments made over the past several years in capacity expansion, innovation, commercial capabilities and productportfolio diversification translated into broad-based growth across geographies, improved profitability and a stronger business mix.
 The Company delivered consolidated revenue growth of ~13.0% during the year, while EBITDA grew ~15.8%, with EBITDA margin
improving to ~20.4%. This performance was driven by strong execution across regions, an improving product mix, strong operational discipline and sustained customer demand across key end markets.
 A key highlight of FY26 was the ongoing transformation of EPL’s portfolio. Beauty & Cosmetics delivered record growth of approximately 
30%, while Oral Care returned to healthy growth of around 3.4%. As a result, Personal Care & Beyond now accounts for 53% of theCompany’s tube revenue, reflecting the success of EPL’s strategic focus on diversifying beyond its traditional Oral Care business andbroadening its presence in faster-growing categories.
 The Company’s investments in manufacturing capacity and innovation translated into stronger regional capabilities and supported
future growth. During the year, EPL commissioned its new manufacturing facility in Thailand, strengthening its presence in theEAP region, while the Brazil facility continued to scale up and emerged as a meaningful contributor to growth in the Americas.
These investments further enhance the Company’s ability to serve customers through a diversified manufacturing footprint andsupport future growth opportunities.
 The Company also delivered consistent operational performance through the year, recording four consecutive quarters of double-
digit revenue growth, culminating in ~17.6% revenue growth in the fourth quarter - the highest quarterly growth achieved in the last five years. This performance reflects the resilience of EPL’s business model, strong customer trust and the Company’s ability to translate long-term strategic investments into sustainable and profitable growth.
5. FINANCIAL AND OPER ATIONAL PERFORMANCE: FY26
 The Company’s financial performance during FY26 reflected the successful execution of its growth strategy, with broad-based revenue 
growth translating into improved profitability and stronger returns. Consolidated revenue from operations increased by ~13.0% to
` 47,631 Million in FY26, while EBITDA grew by ~15.8% to ` 9,724 Million, resulting in an EBITDA margin of ~20.4%, an improvement
of 49 basis points over the previous year.
 The improvement in profitability was supported by a favourable product mix, led by continued growth in the higher-value Beauty &
Cosmetics segment, operating leverage from increased volumes, disciplined cost management and ongoing productivity initiativesacross manufacturing operations. EBITDA margins remained above 20% for seven consecutive quarters, reflecting the Company’ssustained focus on profitable growth.
 Profit After Tax (excluding exceptional items) increased by ~15.0% to ` 4,171 Million, while reported PAT stood at ` 3,889 Million. 
The Company’s financial position improved during the year, with the net debt-to-EBITDA ratio improving to 0.52x, reflectingdisciplined capital allocation and healthy cash generation. Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) improved to ~19.0%, demonstratingthe Company’s continued focus on enhancing capital efficiency while investing for future growth.
6. SEGMENT-WISE PERFORMANCE  HIGHLIGHTS
 EPL operates through f our geographic regions - AMESA, EAP , Americas and Europe, providing a diversified revenue base and enabling 
the Company to serve customers through local manufacturing, regional agility and strong customer partnerships. FY26 witnessedbroad-based growth across all regions, reflecting the benefits of portfolio diversification, capacity investments and disciplinedexecution.

Management Discussion and Analysis (contd.) AMESA
  The AMESA region delivered a resilient performance during FY26, with revenue growing ~5.1% and EBITDA margin improving to 
~18.7%. Growth was supported by steady demand in Oral Care, improving momentum in Personal Care & Beyond and continued 
focus on operational efficiency. The region also strengthened its export footprint while continuing to deepen relationships with key customers across India, the Middle East and Africa.
 EAP
  The EAP region delivered another year of strong performance, with revenue growing ~15.7% and EBITDA increasing ~20.9%, resulting 
in an EBITDA margin of ~22.1%. Despite macroeconomic headwinds in certain markets, the region benefited from continued customer additions, a favourable product mix and strong momentum in Beauty & Cosmetics and extruded tubes,
  A key milestone during the year was the commissioning of EPL’s manufacturing facility in Thailand, strengthening the Company’s 
presence in the ASEAN region. Together with continued investments in innovation and customer engagement, this further enhances EPL’s ability to serve customers with greater agility and positions the region for long-term growth.
 Americas
  The Americas was one of the strongest-performing regions during the year, delivering revenue growth of ~21.1% and EBITDA growth 
of ~37.1%, with EBITDA margin improving to ~20.5%. The strong performance reflected broad-based growth across the countries, supported by disciplined execution, new customer additions and an improving product mix.
  A defining featur e of the year was the evolving tariff environment in the United States. Leveraging its local manufacturing footprint 
and agile supply chain, the Company successfully navigated these challenges while ensuring uninterrupted customer service and supply continuity, without compromising profitability. The region, in fact, delivered significant margin expansion during the year, reflecting the strength of its operating model and disciplined cost management.
  The Brazil facility continued its successful ramp-up and emerged as an important contributor to regional growth, while the United 
States, Mexico and Colombia also delivered healthy business performance. Together, these market-specific successes reinforced the Americas’ position as EPL’s strongest-performing region during FY26.
 Europe
  Europe delivered revenue growth of ~10.4% during FY26. However, EBITDA declined by ~3.2%, with EBITDA margin at ~14.5%, 
reflecting a challenging operating environment for the region.
  The Company remained focused on improving the region’s operating performance through productivity initiatives, disciplined cost 
management and stronger commercial execution. Continued emphasis on customer engagement, operational excellence and growth in higher-value categories is expected to support a gradual improvement in profitability over the medium term.
7. BUSINESS STR ATEGY
  EPL’s long-term strategy is anchored in its 4X4 framework, comprising four strategic pillars—Category, Customers, Country and Cost—
supported by four key enablers: Innovation, Agile Sales & Marketing, Digital Transformation and One EPL Culture. Consistent execution of this strategy enabled the Company to deliver ~13.0% revenue growth, ~15.8% EBITDA growth and an EBITDA margin of ~20.4% during FY26, while strengthening its long-term competitive position.
 Category
  EPL strengthened its leadership in Oral Care while accelerating growth in faster-growing categories. During FY26, Beauty & Cosmetics 
delivered record growth of approximately 30%, while Oral Care returned to healthy growth of around 3.4%. Over the past few years, the Company has invested in manufacturing capacity and front-end commercial capabilities to build differentiated offerings for this segment, including expanding its extruded tube portfolio, Neo Seam technology and other value-added packaging solutions. These investments have broadened EPL’s ability to address the growing Beauty & Cosmetics market and contributed to the continued transformation of its portfolio, with Personal Care & Beyond now accounting for 53% of tube revenue.

 Innovation

  Digital Transformation enhances operational excellence across EPL’s global manufacturing network. During FY26, the Company 
invested in advanced manufacturing technologies, automation and digital tools to enhance productivity, quality and decision-making across operations.  Leveraging the Power of One EPL

This collaborative approach enables the Company to respond faster to customer needs, scale successful initiatives across regions and build organisational capabilities that support long-term sustainable growth.

Management Discussion and Analysis (contd.)8. CORPORATE DEVELOPMENT: PROPOSED MERGER WITH INDOVIDA
  The proposed merger with Indovida India Private Limited (“Indovida”) marks a transformational milestone in EPL’s journey to build a 
diversified consumer packaging platform for emerging markets.
  Announced in Mar ch 2026, the transaction combines EPL’s leadership in laminated and tube packaging with Indovida’s scale in rigid 
PET packaging through a scheme of amalgamation under which EPL will remain the listed entity. The combined business is expected 
to generate annual revenues of ~US$1 billion, with nearly 75% of revenues derived from emerging markets. Upon completion, 
Indorama Ventures is expected to become a co-promoter of the Company with a ~51.8% shareholding, while Blackstone will hold  
~16.6% shareholding.
  The proposed combination advances EPL’s ambition of building a leading consumer packaging platform for emerging markets by 
bringing together complementary product portfolios, customer relationships and manufacturing footprints. The merger expands EPL’s 
presence across multiple packaging formats, creating opportunities for cross-selling, deeper customer engagement and accelerated geographic expansion, particularly across South-east Asia and Africa. Procurement, supply chain and sustainability synergies are also expected to strengthen the combined platform, while building on EPL’s successful experience of commissioning and scaling new manufacturing facilities.
  Beyond the strategic benefits, the transaction is expected to further strengthen EPL’s financial profile. Indovida is a net-cash business 
and the combined entity is expected to benefit from a stronger balance sheet, improved financial flexibility and enhanced capacity to pursue future organic and inorganic growth opportunities. The transaction is expected to be earnings accretive, while also improving profitability and return ratios through procurement, supply chain and operational synergies. The combined organisation will also benefit from Indorama Ventures’ global scale, manufacturing expertise and proven acquisition track record, providing a strong platform for long-term value creation.
  Subject to the requisite shareholder, regulatory and judicial approvals, the proposed merger is expected to position EPL as a leading 
consumer packaging platform focused on emerging markets, with a broader product portfolio, stronger geographic presence and enhanced capabilities to deliver sustainable long-term growth.
9. OPPORTUNITIES
  EPL is well positioned t o capitalise on the structural shifts reshaping the global packaging industry. The Company’s diversified 
manufacturing footprint, differentiated product portfolio and long-standing customer relationships provide a strong foundation to capture growth opportunities across categories, geographies and packaging formats.
  Beauty & Cosmetics  continues to represent the largest growth opportunity for the Company. Rising consumer preference for 
premium, functional and aesthetically differentiated packaging, coupled with increasing demand from regional and emerging brands, is driving strong growth across this segment. EPL’s investments in extruded tubes, applicator solutions, advanced printing capabilities and specialised commercial teams position the Company to further strengthen its leadership in this high-growth category.
  Sustainable packaging  presents significant long-term opportunities as customers accelerate the transition towards recyclable and 
circular packaging solutions. With recyclable formats accounting for 39% of tube sales during FY26 and a portfolio of innovative solutions such as Platina and r-Platina, EPL is well positioned to support customers in meeting evolving regulatory requirements and sustainability commitments.
  The Company also sees significant opportunities to expand its presence across high-growth emerging markets, supported 
by its diversified manufacturing footprint and investments in regional capacity. The commissioning of the Thailand facility and the continued ramp-up of the Brazil facility further strengthen EPL’s ability to serve customers closer to their markets while supporting future expansion across Southeast Asia, Latin America and other attractive growth markets.
  As the business scales, EPL expects to further strengthen profitability through a combination of favourable product mix, higher 
capacity utilisation and sustained operational excellence initiatives. The growing contribution of higher-value categories such as Beauty & Cosmetics, coupled with ongoing investments in manufacturing efficiency, procurement and automation, provides a strong foundation for sustained margin expansion. Having consistently improved profitability over the past several years, EPL remains focused on ensuring that earnings growth continues to outpace revenue growth while maintaining disciplined investments behind future expansion.
  Subject to the necessary approvals, the proposed merger with Indovida  has the potential to significantly enhance EPL’s long-
term growth prospects by expanding its product portfolio into rigid PET packaging, broadening its customer offering and creating a diversified consumer packaging platform for emerging markets. The combined entity is expected to benefit from complementary capabilities, greater scale and enhanced opportunities for cross-selling, innovation and geographic expansion.

Management Discussion and Analysis (contd.)10. SUST AINABILITY
  Sustainability is embedded in EPL’s strategy and is integral to the way the Company innovates, manufactures and partners with 
customers. As sustainability becomes a defining priority for global consumer brands and regulators alike, EPL strengthens its 
capabilities to deliver packaging solutions that combine recyclability, performance and aesthetics, helping customers advance their own sustainability commitments.
  FY26 mark ed a significant milestone in the Company’s sustainability agenda with the achievement of an EcoVadis Platinum rating, 
placing EPL among the top 1% of more than 150,000 companies assessed globally on ESG performance. This recognition reflects the Company’s continued commitment to embedding sustainability across its operations, products and governance, while reinforcing its position as a trusted partner for customers seeking more sustainable packaging solutions.
  Building on this foundation, EPL expanded its por tfolio of sustainable packaging solutions. During FY26, recyclable tubes accounted 
for 39% of tube sales, up from 33% in FY25, supported by investments in manufacturing capabilities and product innovation. Solutions such as Platina and r-Platina meet the recyclability requirements of the European Union’s Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR), enabling customers to transition towards more circular packaging without compromising performance or aesthetics.
  The Company also advanced its broader sustainability commitments through its Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi), continued 
recognition by the Ellen MacArthur Foundation and sustained focus on reducing the environmental footprint of its operations. Sustainability has evolved from a compliance imperative into a source of competitive advantage, strengthening customer partnerships, driving innovation-led growth and creating long-term value for all stakeholders.
11. HUMAN RESOURCES
  People remain at the heart of EPL’s long-term success and competitive advantage. The Company is committed to fostering a high-
performance, purpose-driven and inclusive workplace where employees are empowered to innovate, collaborate and grow. Its people strategy is anchored around five pillars-organization structures enabling growth, new capabilities building, culture and engagement, diversity and inclusion, and talent development-ensuring that the organisation remains equipped to support its long-term growth ambitions. With 6000+ workforce, with 23 nationalities, our teams across the world are taking our vision forward everyday. 
  During FY26, EPL strengthened its position as an employer of choice, earning Great Place to Work® certification across seven countries. 
Women represented 32% of the Company’s global workforce, while EPL accelerated inclusion efforts by employing over 150 persons with disabilities globally, reinforcing its commitment to building a diverse and inclusive workplace.
  The Company invested in capability building through structured learning and development programmes, cross-functional 
collaboration and leadership development initiatives. Employee wellbeing framework is well established across markets, which enables wellbeing across financial, emotional, physical and social wellbeing. This strengthens organisational culture, while a merit-based performance management system supported high performance and career growth. As the Company continues to invest in innovation, digital capabilities and sustainability, it remains focused on building a future-ready workforce equipped to support the next phase of growth.
12. FINANCE
  EPL maintained a disciplined financial approach dur ing FY26, balancing investments in growth with a continued focus on cash 
generation, capital efficiency and balance sheet strength. This prudent approach enabled the Company to fund strategic capacity expansion, invest in innovation and further strengthen its financial position while maintaining a conservative leverage profile.
  As at March 31, 2026, consolidated net debt stood at ` 5,017 million, an increase of ` 449 million over the previous year, reflecting 
disciplined investments in strategic growth initiatives. Despite this, the Company maintained a healthy debt-to-equity ratio of 0.25 (0.29 in FY25), while the Debt Service Coverage Ratio (DSCR) improved significantly to 3.98 (2.62 in FY25), demonstrating the Company’s strong debt servicing capability and healthy operating cash flows. Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) improved to ~19.0%, from ~18.0% in FY25, supported by higher profitability and improved asset utilisation.
  The Company’s strong financial profile was recognised by leading rating agencies. During the year, CARE Ratings reaffirmed EPL’s 
long-term and short-term credit ratings at CARE AA+ (Stable) and CARE A1+, respectively. India Ratings & Research (Fitch Group) also reaffirmed the Company’s issuer rating at IND AA+ (Stable) and its short-term rating at IND A1+. These reaffirmations reflect confidence in the Company’s financial strength, prudent capital allocation and resilient operating performance.
  Looking ahead, the Company remains focused on maintaining a strong balance sheet, improving return ratios and deploying capital 
prudently to support both organic growth and strategic opportunities. This disciplined financial framework provides the flexibility to invest behind long-term growth while maintaining resilience in a dynamic operating environment.

Management Discussion and Analysis (contd.)13. RISK MANAGEMENT
  The Company operates in a dynamic and globally integrated industry, making it susceptible to a range of strategic, operational 
and external risks. EPL’s risk management framework is designed to proactively identify, assess and mitigate these risks, embedding 
risk management into business planning, decision-making and day-to-day operations. The Company’s diversified manufacturing footprint, disciplined operating model and strong governance framework enhance its ability to navigate an increasingly complex business environment.
 External Risks
  Macroeconomic Volatility:  Inflationary pressures, foreign exchange fluctuations, changing consumer demand and slower economic 
growth across key markets could impact demand for packaged products and influence input costs. The Company closely monitors macroeconomic developments while maintaining a disciplined approach to pricing, cost management and capital allocation.
  Geopolitical and Trade Risks: Ongoing geopolitical conflicts, evolving trade policies and tariff-related developments have increased 
uncertainty across global supply chains. EPL’s diversified manufacturing network across more than 21 facilities in 11 countries enables regional production and supply flexibility, strengthening business continuity and helping the Company respond effectively to changing trade dynamics while maintaining high customer service levels.
  Climate and Sustainability Risks:  Increasing regulatory focus on sustainability, Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) regulations 
and evolving customer expectations shape the packaging industry. EPL remains well positioned through its investments in sustainable packaging solutions, with the Company’s recyclable product mix increasing to 39% during FY26, while continuing to advance innovation in materials and manufacturing processes.
  Competitive and Market Dynamics:  Consumer preferences, packaging formats and customer requirements have evolved rapidly, 
particularly in Beauty & Cosmetics and sustainable packaging. Maintaining leadership requires continuous investment in innovation, differentiated products, commercial capabilities and manufacturing technologies. EPL addresses these evolving market dynamics through sustained investments in product innovation, customer partnerships and expansion into higher-growth categories.
 Operational Risks
  Customer Concentration:  While the Company enjoys long-standing relationships with leading global FMCG companies, a significant 
portion of revenue continues to be derived from key customers. EPL mitigates this risk by expanding its presence across Beauty & Cosmetics and other Personal Care categories, increasing engagement with regional and emerging brands, and broadening its customer base across geographies and end-use segments.
  Raw Material Availability and Cost: The availability and pricing of key raw materials, particularly polymers, remain influenced 
by crude oil prices, supply-demand dynamics and global logistics. The Company mitigates these risks through strategic supplier partnerships, multi-source procurement, disciplined inventory management, productivity initiatives and commercial actions to minimise the impact of raw material volatility.
  Cybersecurity and Data Privacy: As EPL strengthens its digital capabilities, cybersecurity and data privacy remain key priorities. The 
Company maintains a robust information security framework, supported by ISO 27001 standards, regular risk assessments, employee awareness programmes and continued investments in cybersecurity and digital resilience.
  Risk management at EPL is embedded within the Company’s strategy and operating model, enabling informed decision-making across 
all levels of the organisation. Through continuous monitoring, strong governance, disciplined execution and proactive mitigation, the Company remains well positioned to navigate an increasingly dynamic business environment while delivering sustainable, profitable growth.
14. INTERNAL C ONTROL SYSTEMS AND THEIR ADEQUACY
  The Company has implemented a robust internal control framework and a structured internal audit process to ensure the integrity 
of its financial reporting, strengthen operational controls, safeguard its assets and ensure compliance with applicable laws and regulations. These controls are embedded across key business and accounting processes and are periodically reviewed to enhance their effectiveness and support the Company’s evolving business requirements.
  The Audit Committee of the Board plays a pivotal role in overseeing the Company’s internal control framework. During the year, the 
Audit Committee, in consultation with the Internal Auditor, reviewed and approved the scope and coverage of the internal audit programme. Comprehensive internal audits were conducted across the Company’s global operations, along with focused reviews of 
application controls and other critical business processes. The findings from these audits are regularly reviewed by Management, with the Audit Committee and Statutory Auditors being periodically apprised of key observations and the progress of corrective actions, ensuring continuous improvement and accountability.

15. OUTL OOK
  EPL enters F inancial Year 2026-27 (“FY27”) from a position of strength, having delivered broad-based growth, improved profitability 
and further strengthening of its business fundamentals. The Company believes that the structural trends shaping the packaging industry-including premiumisation, sustainability, the increasing relevance of Beauty & Cosmetics and the shift towards differentiated packaging solutions-continue to provide a favourable backdrop for long-term growth.
  Against this backdrop, EPL will remain focused on executing its strategic priorities. The Company will strengthen its presence in 
higher-growth categories, deepen customer relationships, expand in attractive geographies and invest in innovation, manufacturing capabilities and commercial excellence. Alongside growth, continued emphasis on operational excellence, productivity initiatives and disciplined capital allocation will remain central to enhancing competitiveness and creating long-term value.
  The Company also remains conscious of the evolving global operating environment. Geopolitical developments, including the 
ongoing conflict in the Middle East, together with evolving trade policies and macroeconomic uncertainty, continue to present challenges for global supply chains and input costs. EPL’s diversified manufacturing footprint, regional operating model and disciplined risk management framework provide the resilience and flexibility to respond to these developments while ensuring supply continuity and maintaining high levels of customer service.
  Subject to the requisite shareholder, regulatory and judicial approvals, the proposed merger with Indovida is expected to be the 
Company’s most significant strategic milestone in FY27 and beyond. The proposed combination will create a diversified consumer packaging platform with complementary product portfolios, a broader geographic footprint and enhanced capabilities, positioning the Company for its next phase of growth.
  Looking ahead, EPL remains committed to consist ently delivering sustained double-digit growth while maintaining EBITDA margins 
above 20% and steadily improving returns on capital. As it continues to expand its capabilities, deepen customer partnerships and 
execute with discipline, the Company remains well positioned to shape the future of sustainable consumer packaging and create lasting value for all stakeholders.

4.  SCHEME OF  AMALGAMATION (BY WAY OF MERGER BY ABSORPTION) OF INDOVIDA INDIA PRIVATE LIMITED 
(“INDOVIDA”) WITH THE COMPANY AND THEIR RESPECTIVE SHAREHOLDERS
  During the year under review, the Board, based on the recommendations of the Audit Committee and the Committee of Independent 
Directors, approved the Scheme of Amalgamation (by way of merger by absorption) of Indovida with the Company and their respective shareholders, pursuant to Sections 230 to 232 and other applicable provisions of the Act, the SEBI LODR Regulations and other applicable laws (“Proposed Merger”). 
  The Proposed Merger represents a strategic step aligned with the Company’s long-term growth vision of becoming a leading 
consumer packaging partner across emerging markets, as it is expected to combine the Company’s leadership in specialty flexible packaging with Indovida’s strong presence in rigid packaging solutions, thereby expanding the combined entity’s product portfolio, customer coverage and geographic footprint across key emerging markets.
  The Proposed Merger is expected to strengthen the Company’s ability to offer a wider range of products through the combined 
operations of the Company and Indovida, while enhancing geographical diversification and operational, organisational and financial efficiencies. It is also expected to support cost optimisation and synergies through pooling of resources, facilitate an integrated approach to financial consolidation, capital allocation and cash management, enable adoption of best practices and process automation, and strengthen organisational capability and leadership by bringing together diverse skills, talent and experience to drive operational excellence and sustained value creation for stakeholders.
  Upon effec tiveness of the Proposed Merger, which is subject to the requisite regulatory and statutory approvals, the Company will 
continue as the listed entity. Also, on effectiveness of the Proposed Merger, the Company shall issue and allot to each shareholder of Indovida 286 fully Paid-up Equity Shares of face value ` 2 each of the Company, for every 10,000 fully Paid-up Equity Shares of face 
value ` 10 each held by such shareholder in Indovida. The share exchange ratio for the Proposed Merger has been determined on the 
joint valuation report dated March 28, 2026, issued by BDO Valuation Advisory LLP and D and P India Advisory Services, Independent Registered Valuers. Ernst & Young Merchant Banking Services LLP , a SEBI registered Category-I Merchant Banker, has issued its fairness opinion dated March 28, 2026, confirming on the fairness of the aforesaid share exchange ratio.
  Further details in relation to the Proposed Merger are available on the website of the Company i.e. at https://www.eplglobal.com/
investors/scheme-of-amalgamation/.

12. INTERNAL A UDIT AND INTERNAL FINANCIAL CONTROLS 
 Internal Audit 
  The Company has established a robust and comprehensive framework for Internal Financial Controls, integrating internal audit, 
enterprise risk management, and compliance monitoring. The internal control environment is strengthened by an independent Internal Audit function, which is supported by a network of external audit firms to enhance coverage and expertise.
  In line with its governance responsibilities, the Audit Committee annually approves a risk-based Internal Audit Plan. This plan 
encompasses key risks and controls across manufacturing units, offices, warehouses, and centrally managed functions. The Audit Committee, on a quarterly basis, reviews significant audit observations and the status of remediation actions, ensuring timely resolution and continuous improvement. Further, it also reviews the final reports on audit findings, follow-up actions, and the overall internal control environment, on an annual basis.
 Internal Financial Controls (“IFC”)
  The IFC framework of the Company is aligned with the principles of the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway 
Commission (COSO) and is commensurate with the scale and complexity of the Company’s operations, thereby meeting the requirements of the Act. It is anchored in the ‘three lines of defence’ model and supported by well-defined Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and policy framework. The Management of the Company, along with Statutory and Internal Auditors, conducts periodic testing of controls to assess both design adequacy and operating effectiveness. 
  During the year under review, the IFC framework was independently assessed in accordance with the guidelines issued by the Institute 
of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI), and the review confirmed that the Internal Financial Controls are satisfactory in both design and operational effectiveness.
  More details on the Company’s Internal Control Systems, including Internal Financial Controls, are provided in the ‘Management 
Discussion and Analysis’ section, which forms part of the Integrated Annual Report, separately.
 Risk Management 
  Risk Management is deeply embedded within the governance architecture of the Company, and it is treated as a strategic enabler that 
supports its long-term vision, rather than just a defence mechanism against uncertainties. 
  The Company’s Business Risk Assessment (BRA) processes enable periodic self-assessment of business risks, operating controls, and 
compliance with corporate policies, which facilitates continuous monitoring of evolving risks and the effectiveness of mitigation measures. The Internal Audit function provides independent and objective assurance to the Management and the Board, on the effectiveness of risk management and internal control systems. The use of data analytics further enhances audit depth, coverage, and efficiency. Proactive fraud risk assessments are also undertaken across key functions to identify control vulnerabilities.
  The Board has also constituted the Risk Management Committee (“RMC”) in terms of the provisions of Regulation 21 of SEBI LODR 
Regulations, for reviewing the risks and mitigation measures on a periodic basis. All aspects of risk, such as strategic, regulatory and compliance, operational, financial and reputational risks, whether internal or external, are discussed in the meeting(s) of the RMC. Details of the composition of the RMC along with the details of participation of the Members at its meetings and the terms of reference of RMC are disclosed in the ‘Corporate Governance Report’ of the Company for the year under review, which forms part of the Integrated Annual Report, separately.Board’s Report (contd.)

  The structured Risk Management process of the Company spans the entire risk lifecycle, i.e. identification of risks that could adversely

15. RELATED PARTY TRANSACTIONS I.E. CONTRACTS AND ARRANGEMENT WITH RELATED PARTIES
  In line with the requirements of the Act and the applicable provisions of the SEBI LODR Regulations, the Company has formulated a 
policy on dealing with Related Party Transactions (“RPTs”). The Policy intends to ensure that proper reporting, approval and disclosure 
processes are in place for all transactions between the Company and its related parties.
  All transactions with r elated parties during the year under review were in accordance with the Policy on RPT formulated by the 
Company. Further, all arrangements or transactions entered by the Company during the year under review with related parties were conducted on an ‘arm’s length’ basis and in the ordinary course of business. Prior omnibus approval was obtained for RPTs which were of repetitive nature, were entered in the ordinary course of business and were at arm’s length. 24. INVESTOR  EDUCATION AND PROTECTION FUND (“IEPF”) 
  In terms of the applicable provisions of the Act, read with the Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority (Accounting, Audit, 
Transfer and Refund) Rules, 2016 (as amended) (“IEPF Rules”), all dividends which are lying unpaid or unclaimed for a period of  
7 (seven) years, are required to be transferred by the Company to the IEPF, established by the Government of India, after the completion 
of 7 (seven) years. Further, in terms of the IEPF Rules, the Equity Shares on which the dividend has remained unpaid or unclaimed for 7 (seven) consecutive years or more shall also be transferred to the demat account of the IEPF Authority. 
  During the year, the Company transferred an amount of ` 13,55,429 representing the unclaimed and unpaid dividend pertaining 
to Financial Year 2017-18 to the IEPF. Further, 1,05,584 Equity Shares of the Company, to which such dividend pertained, were also transferred to IEPF Authority, as per the requirements of the IEPF Rules.
  The Company regularly sends reminders to those members whose dividends have remained unclaimed, thereby requesting them to 
update the bank account details with Registrar and Transfer Agents (RTA)/ Depository Participants/Company, to ensure timely credit of Dividends by the Company. The members can claim the shares transferred to the IEPF Authority along with the dividend(s) by making an application to IEPF Authority in accordance with the procedure available on www.iepf.gov.in and on submission of such 
documents as prescribed under the IEPF Rules. 
  Details of the unpaid/ unclaimed dividend along with the names of the Members to whom such dividend pertains, are available on 
the website of the Company i.e. at https://www.eplglobal.com/investors/shareholder-information/.
  Mr. Onkar Ghangurde, Head - Legal, Company Secretary & Compliance Officer of the Company is appointed as the Nodal Officer under 
Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority (Accounting, Audit, Transfer and Refund) Rules, 2016. Details of the Nodal Officer are available on the website of the Company i.e. at https://www.eplglobal.com/investors/shareholder-information/.

PARTICULARS WITH RESPECT TO CONSERVATION OF ENERGY , TECHNOLOGY ABSORPTION AND FOREIGN EXCHANGE 
EARNINGS AND OUTGO AS PRESCRIBED UNDER THE COMPANIES (ACCOUNTS) RULES, 2014
A. CONSERVATION OF ENERGY
i. Steps taken or impact on conservation of energy:
  As part of its sustainability agenda, during the financial year ended on March 31, 2026 (“year under review”/ “Financial 
Year 2025-26”), EPL Limited (“Company”) continued to focus on energy conservation, as a key pillar of its operational 
sustainability strategy through targeted actions for utility optimisation, process improvements and clean energy solutions.  
These initiatives not only contributed to lower energy usage but also strengthened the resilience and sustainability across the Company’s manufacturing footprint.
 A summary of the initiativ es undertaken during the year under review, is as under:
 (a)  At the Nalagarh Unit, the Compressed Air Line and its volume were optimized to suit the total requirement of the Unit, including 
the additional tubing lines installed, which yielded energy saving benefits of 78,000 kWh per month (i.e. a total energy saving of 9,36,000 kWh during the year under review); 
 (b)  At the Goa Unit, optimisation of chiller temperature settings within the HVAC system enhanced energy efficiency and delivered 
savings of approximately 3,301 kWh per month (i.e. 39,612 kWh during the year under review); and
 (c)  The Vasind Unit achieved significant energy savings through optimisation of cooling tower operations and deployment of solar 
air-conditioning systems for the UPS room, yielding savings of 8,400 kWh per month (i.e. total energy saving of 1,00,800 kWh during the year under review).
  In the next financial year i.e. Financial Year 2026-27, the Company proposes to undertake utility upgrades at its Nalagarh and Manpura 
Units, such as implementation of energy-efficient room cooling and process chiller systems, installation of high-efficiency chillers and air compressors, and engineering design enhancements. These initiatives are expected to generate additional energy savings of approximately 350,000 kWh per month (equivalent to 4.2 Million kWh annually).
ii.  Steps taken by the Company for utilizing alternate sources of energy:
  During the year under review, the Company procured 14,85,066 kWh of wind energy from EnergyEdge Power Trading Private Limited 
for its units located at Wada and Vasind, in Maharashtra, which accounted for ~2.4% of the total electricity consumption across all units of the Company in India.
  Further, upon commencement of supply of solar and wind energy to its units located at Vapi (Gujarat) and Vasind and Wada 
(Maharashtra), by virtue of the Energy Supply Agreements entered into by the Company with Clean Max Aria Private Limited under group captive arrangement, it is expected that renewable energy will contribute to ~65-70% of the Company’s annual energy requirements, thereby significantly enhancing the share of renewable energy in its overall energy mix.
iii. The capital investment on energy conservation equipment:
  The Company has invested ~ ` 9 Million in energy conservation equipment and systems at its units located at Nalagarh, Manpura, and 
Vasind.
B. TECHNOLOGY  ABSORPTION
i. Efforts made towards technology absorption:
 (a) Circular E conomy and Material Optimisation
   During the y ear under review, the Company strengthened its circular economy initiatives by collaborating with leading global 
material suppliers and technology partners to optimise multilayer packaging structures through source reduction. A key focus area in this regard was optimisation of Ethylene Vinyl Alcohol (EVOH) layers, where extensive design iterations and product trials enabled a reduction in material usage while maintaining the required oxygen barrier performance. These solutions were successfully validated with select customers, demonstrating sustainable material innovation without compromising product functionality.
 (b) Expansion of Barr ier Film Capabilities
   Further, the Company enhanced its barrier film manufacturing capabilities through commissioning of a second 9-layer blown 
film line at its Vasind Unit. This strategic investment strengthened localisation, improved supply chain resilience and enhanced manufacturing flexibility. In parallel, the Company optimised its barrier structure portfolio to facilitate efficient production across multiple specifications while reducing resin losses during transition phases, thereby supporting both cost efficiency and circular economy objectives.Annexure D
159
Statutory Reports
=== page 98 ===
 (c) Sustainable Metalliz ed Laminate Innovation
   The Company strengthened its innovation pipeline in metallized laminates through collaborations with key machinery partners. 
Focused initiatives enabled the development of sustainable metallized structures that deliver premium visual appeal, including 
high gloss and metallic sheen, essential for cosmetic packaging. These advancements allow entry into new high-value markets while balancing sustainability goals with aesthetic performance and have been successfully taken forward for customer evaluations.
ii. Benefits derived like product improvement, cost reduction, product development or import substitution:
 (a)  With sustainabilit y at the forefront, the Company has significantly advanced its Post-Consumer Recycled resins (“PCR”) integration 
strategy by broadening and validating multiple recycled resin sources. This led to enhanced cost saving, quality consistency and performance of PCR laminates, enabling reliable scale-up across applications.
 (b)  The Company has localized PCR sourcing in key markets, supporting circular economy objectives while improving supply 
resilience. These efforts have enabled the Company to deliver tubes with up to 60% mechanically recycled PCR content (by weight), contributing meaningfully to customers’ carbon reduction goals.
 (c)  During the y ear under review, the Company strengthened its material sourcing strategy by working closely with key raw 
material partners to develop and qualify a broader range of domestic resin alternatives. This wider and more resilient supply base enabled the Company to successfully manage supply chain challenges arising from recent global disruptions, while improving responsiveness, reducing lead times, and maintaining cost competitiveness in its tube offerings.

Corporate Governance Report
1. COMPANY’S PHILOSOPHY ON CORPORATE GOVERNANCE
  At EPL Limited (“EPL” or “the Company”), Corporate Governance underpins institutional integrity, stakeholder trust, organisational 
resilience, and sustainable long-term value creation. The Company is committed to maintaining the highest standards of Corporate 
Governance and ethical business conduct through transparency in decision-making, accountability in performance, fairness in stakeholder engagement, and responsible stewardship of resources.
  The Company’s governance philosophy is founded on six principles: transparency, independence, accountability, responsibility, 
fairness, and social responsibility. These principles are embedded in its policies, processes, internal controls, risk management systems, and operating practices, and guide the conduct of the Board of Directors of the Company (“Board”), Management, and employees. They foster a culture of integrity and professionalism and reinforce stakeholder confidence.
  The Board provides strategic direction, exercises effective oversight, guides Management, and ensures accountability to stakeholders. 
The Company is professionally managed within a framework of clearly defined roles, responsibilities, and delegated authority, ensuring that decisions are taken transparently, responsibly, and with due regard to stakeholder expectations and the Company’s broader societal responsibilities.
  As a responsible global enterprise, the Company aligns its governance practices with applicable laws and regulations, evolving 
stakeholder expectations, and recognised governance standards. Sound governance is institutionalised across the Company and its subsidiaries through robust policies, effective oversight mechanisms, and a strong compliance framework. This framework is reviewed and strengthened regularly to support prudent decision-making, responsible growth, organisational resilience, and sustainable value creation.
  The Company adheres to the Corporate Governance requirements stipulated under the Companies Act, 2013 read with the applicable 
rules made thereunder (“Act”) and the provisions of Regulations 17-27 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“SEBI LODR Regulations”).
 Code of Conduct for Board Members and Senior Management
  The Company has adopted a Code of Conduct for its Directors and Employees, which requires adherence to lawful and ethical 
business practices at all times. The Code of Conduct reinforces Corporate Governance as a cornerstone of sustainable performance and responsible stakeholder engagement, fostering a culture of integrity and ethical behaviour in all business dealings.
  The Code is, inter alia,  applicable to all Directors and Senior Management Personnel, and is available on the website of the Company 
at https://www.eplglobal.com/investors/corporate-governance/.
  The Company has received a declaration of compliance with the Code of Conduct from Directors and Senior Management Personnel. 
The declaration by the Managing Director affirming adherence to the Code of Conduct by the Board of Directors and Senior Management Personnel is appended to this Report.
 Code of Conduct for Prohibition of Insider Trading
  The Company has adopted a Code of Conduct to regulate, monitor and report trading by Insiders/ Designated Persons  in terms of the 
applicable provisions of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 (as amended).
 Integrated Reporting and ESG Disclosures
  In alignment with its commitment to transparency, accountability, and long-term stakeholder value, the Company has voluntarily 
published this, 2nd Integrated Annual Report for the financial year ended on March 31, 2026 (“Financial Year 2025-26”/ “year under 
review”), which provides a comprehensive overview of the Company’s financial and non-financial performance. Further, in compliance with Regulation 34(2)(f ) of the SEBI LODR Regulations, the Company has published its Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report 
(BRSR), as a part of the Integrated Annual Report, which outlines its perfo rmance across key Environmental, Social, and Governance 
(ESG) dimensions. These disclosures underscore the Company’s commitment to responsible business practices and demonstrate its alignment with evolving regulatory requirements and global best standards.

 Evaluation of performance: Board, Committees and Individual Directors
  In terms of the provisions of Section 178(2) of the Act and the SEBI LODR Regulations, a structured evaluation of the performance of 
the Board, its Committees, the Individual Directors (including Independent Directors), and the Chairman of the Board is undertaken on an annual basis, through a structured questionnaire based on the criteria formulated by the NRC.
  With respect to the year under review, the performance of the Board was assessed on the basis of feedback received from all the 
Directors, on parameters such as Board structure and dynamics, conduct of Board Meetings, strategy, and governance and compliance. The Committees were evaluated on the basis of inputs from their respective members, considering factors such as mandate and composition, effectiveness of Committee Meetings, and contribution to the decisions of the Board. The performance of the Individual Directors (including Independent Directors and the Chairman) was evaluated by the entire Board, excluding the Director being evaluated, on the basis of criteria such as availability and attendance, knowledge and competency, contribution, and integrity and independence. In addition, as mentioned above, the Independent Directors, at a separate meeting, reviewed the performance of the Non-Independent Directors, the Board as a whole.
  The evaluation with respect to the year under review was carried out through a combination of self-evaluation and a 360-degree 
feedback exercise, facilitated through a secure online platform that enabled confidential feedback from the Directors. The rating scale was also refined during the year, enabling sharper differentiation and more meaningful year-on-year benchmarking of performance. The Board further considered the ‘Action Taken Report’ on the feedback received in the previous year, and expressed its satisfaction with the evaluation process and its outcomes, which reflected strong engagement among the Board, its Committees, and the Company’s Management.
